question_text: What are haemozoin granules? What is their significance?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What they are
lines: Inside the red blood cell the malarial parasite
digests the globin part of haemoglobin.
It converts the soluble haem that is left into
steps.why: Haemozoin is the leftover of a meal: the parasite uses the globin as food and cannot use the haem, so the haem is stacked away as an insoluble crystal.
common_mistakes: Writing that the parasite digests the haem. It digests the globin; the haem is left over.
Writing that haemozoin is soluble. It is an insoluble crystalline granule.
steps.memory_tip: Globin is the food, haem is the leftover, and the leftover is haemozoin.
steps.margin_note: Two lines: what is digested, then what is left as granules.

steps.label: Significance

lines.text: Haemozoin release causes the chill and fever

lines: When the red blood cell bursts, the haemozoin is
released into the blood along with the
The released haemozoin causes the chill and
fever of malaria, which return every 48 hours in
steps.why: The significance is the symptom: the fever appears when the cells burst together, which is why the fever of Plasmodium vivax comes back on a fixed 48-hour timetable.
common_mistakes: Writing that haemozoin gives the parasite energy. It is a waste product.
Leaving out the fever. The link to the fever is the whole significance.
steps.memory_tip: Cells burst, pigment out, fever on: that is the 48-hour malaria rhythm.
steps.margin_note: Two lines linking the bursting cell to the fever. Give the 48 hours if you can.

insider_note: The second mark is only for the link to the fever, so the answer must not stop at describing the granule.
